evaluation.final_reason: Immediate practical disputes were settled: Agent A agreed to keep fan/window on and close the door after ten minutes, Agent A agreed not to move Agent C's drying rack without permission, and Agent D's stove-access timing was agreed (call when free). The underlying allocation of long-term ventilation responsibility (the proposed monthly rotation / who 'must' ventilate) was proposed but not finalized, so some substantive disagreement remains.

Agent B moved from insisting cooks must ventilate to accepting immediate measures and a conditional monthly rotation if the smell persists.
Agent C maintained their position about not moving the drying rack; Agent A conceded not to move it without asking.
Agent D shifted to a wait-and-be-called stance and obtained a clear promise from Agent A about notification.

Agent B restates the immediate conditions ('keep the kitchen fan on, leave a kitchen window open, and close the kitchen door after ten minutes') and Agent A reaffirms compliance. Only the future allocation/schedule for ventilation cleaning remains unresolved.

Agent A repeats the same commitments about calling out and keeping the fan/window on. No new substantive conflict arises in this round; the outstanding issue is the not-yet-finalized long-term ventilation responsibility/rotation.

substantive_insights: Tension is mainly between immediate practical mitigation (open window, fan) and protecting others' property (Agent C's drying clothes facing rain).
Agents traded an immediate operational compromise (fan/window on, close door) for an unresolved procedural question (who bears recurring ventilation chores).
Stove-access conflict was resolved by temporal accommodation (Agent D will wait and Agent A will call), showing practical coordination rather than principled victory.
